articles.title: Before buying another single-purpose gadget, chefs recommend these multitasking alternatives
articles.summary: Less is more when it comes to kitchen gear: These versatile cooking companions save space and money.
articles.body:
Our experts independently review everything we recommend. If you buy through our links, we may earn commission.

"My kitchen has too much storage space," said no one, ever. Personally, I'd love some additional cabinets, more countertop real estate and a walk-in pantry. Having been a professional baker, I know firsthand that this isn't just a home cook's plight; commercial kitchens often lack sufficient storage as well. That means chefs have to get creative when it comes to maximizing space, and one way to do that? Relying on multitasking equipment.

Sure, I can appreciate a solid single-use gadget when it saves a lot of time and effort (cherry pitters come to mind). But more often than not, I find that items designed for one niche purpose are gimmicky and not worth the space they take up (banana slicers, anyone?). The next time you think about purchasing a one-and-done kitchen tool, consider these chef-approved workhorses first.

One of my biggest kitchen pet peeves is having drawers that are so jam-packed you can't close them properly. Those little odds and ends really add up, so streamlining smaller essentials makes a big difference.

When I'm prepping food, I want to use as little equipment as possible, which means reaching for versatile tools. This cuts down on the amount of counter space I need and the level of cleanup I'll have to do post-dinner. Sure, necessities like cutting boards and chef's knives might fall under the single-use umbrella, but I don't really count those, as many of us rely on them daily.

As far as meal-prep powerhouses are concerned, my ride-or-die is a humble bench scraper. It's essentially a knife, counter cleaner and frosting smoother (yes, really) in one:

I know, I know, this unassuming tool doesn't look like much — how many uses could it really have? Oh, let me count the ways.

While this bench scraper — also known as a "bench knife" — certainly comes in handy when lifting and portioning out dough, it's so much more than a baker's tool. For starters, it's my go-to for quickly removing residue, flour and food scraps from my counter, making cleanup less taxing, and the blade is dull enough that it won't leave scratch marks. That said, it's sharp enough to cut through many types of vegetables, and when you're finished chopping, you can slide the scraper under the pieces to easily transport them to your pan. I also prefer it to a knife for slicing uniform cubes of cheese and butter, thanks to its straight edge.

Want your cakes to look like they were made by a professional ? I've even used my bench scraper to smooth the frosting after applying it for a clean finish. The more you know!

Accursio Lota, chef/owner of Dora Ristorante in La Jolla, CA, counts vegetable peelers among his multitasking must-haves. "It can be used for vegetables, fruit, salads, vegetable shavings and Parmigiano shavings," he says. Our preferred type here at Yahoo? Y-peelers:

"As a graduate of the French Culinary Institute, I've tried all types of peelers," says one of our kitchen gear testers . "A Y-peeler works much better for me than a straight swivel peeler and is far more comfortable and intuitive in hand. ... I've even been known to gift one when I'm visiting a friend for the weekend — yes, I'm that person who imposes her kitchen gear on others."

The large space below the blades makes it easier to monitor your peeling progress, and because it's used in an up-and-down motion rather than side-to-side, many feel that it puts less strain on wrists and hands.

Step into any professional kitchen, and you're likely to find a Microplane (or six). Peter Ki Suk Tondreau, chef and co-owner/operator of LenLen in New York City, appreciates that it's equally adept at grating "cheese, citrus and garlic," and Matt Sramek, regional executive chef of Southern California's Urban Kitchen Group , calls it "invaluable." "I use it for things like finely grating Parmesan for pasta, zesting fresh lemon onto vegetables and grating fresh garlic without having to chop it with a knife," he explains.

Sure, you could grate cheese using a standard box grater, but having one of these on hand allows you to shave parm right over your food. And it's not just a cheese grater; when I was baking professionally, I'd sometimes have to zest dozens of lemons a day, and this rasp was a game-changer when it came to getting the job done quickly, effectively and safely. (I can't tell you how many times I've nicked myself trying to zest citrus using a box grater, but since this is handheld, it offers much more control.)

I might not be zesting quite as much these days, but I'm still grateful for this gadget every time I'm faced with the task. It earns its keep by grating cheese, chocolate, ginger, garlic and even spices like nutmeg. The brand also recommends using it to shave corks down to fit back into wine bottles or scraping away burnt spots on toast. Who knew?

Once you're ready to cook, simplicity is key; you'll feel less overwhelmed if you only have a handful of gizmos to contend with. Owning fewer tools that give you lots of bang for your buck is better than having a countertop crock that's crowded with every type of spoon and spatula on the market — you simply don't need all of them.

On the spatula front, Tondreau opts for a fish spatula, which will come in clutch even if you're not a fan of seafood:

These turners are ideal for flipping "eggs, veggies, meat and fish," notes Tondreau. Because their stainless steel blades are so thin, they can get under more delicate foods; I also love using them to flip pancakes or eggs without tearing up their edges or to move freshly baked cookies to a cooling rack. The blades are slightly bent, which makes it easier for them to get underneath whatever you're flipping, turning or transferring.

As an Italian-American, a reverence for wooden spoons is probably in my DNA — but it must be a recessive gene, since I haven't used one in years. Yes, they rank highly in the nostalgia department, but after working in professional kitchens, I've concluded that other stirring tools are far more effective, like this one:

Calling it a spatula would be doing it a disservice, so I'm glad the folks at GIR gave this multitasker a more suitable title. True to its name, it's a silicone spoon and spatula in one, and I love it because it's thin and flexible enough to get into the corners of bowls, but also has a spoon-like shape for scooping. I reach for it when I'm folding cake batter, mixing cookie dough or stirring soups and sauces.

It's the sturdiest stirrer (say that five times fast) I've ever used — far more durable than the flimsy plastic spatulas I've tried. Plus, you're essentially getting two tools in one. ( Giada De Laurentiis also swears by this brand.)

Silicone sheet tray liners might seem like one-trick ponies, but I promise they're useful beyond sticky-food prevention — especially if you enjoy baking. (Pie and holiday cookie seasons will be here before we know it…)

I try to minimize waste in the kitchen as much as possible, which is why reusable silicone baking mats come in clutch. Not only do they help keep my parchment paper costs to a minimum, but they also protect my baking sheets from caked-on gunk — and if there's one thing I dread scrubbing, it's a grimy baking sheet.

The nonstick material is a breeze to clean, and I still get a nice golden brown on the bottoms of my cookies when I use it. Plus, I don't have to pry the cookies off once they're out of the oven — they can easily be lifted with a spatula. As for dough that needs to be rolled out, you can do it on one of these rather than your counter to make cleanup a whole lot easier (not to mention, it'll make transferring your pie crust to its baking vessel a breeze).

Cookware often requires the most room in your kitchen, so you'll want to invest wisely. That doesn't always mean splurging on fancy pots and pans; for instance, a stovetop-to-oven cast-iron skillet can be yours for under $30, and I'd argue it can replace nonstick and stainless steel pans if you only have space for one type.

My Lodge skillet is still going strong after over a decade, but these things can last a century. The pan — which is also one of Ina Garten's go-tos — is so sturdy that it can be used on any stove and even over a fire. Because iron is excellent at retaining and distributing heat, nothing will give you a better sear on your steak or crispy exterior on your potatoes. I often go the sweet route, from the literal best chocolate chip pancakes I've ever made to cinnamon rolls and cornbread.

A lot of people are intimidated by cast-iron skillet maintenance, but seasoning is simple. All you need to do is scrub the pan with mild dish soap and warm water, then apply a thin coat of vegetable oil on the inside and outside of the pan. Place it on the top rack of a 450-500°F oven, upside down, with a baking sheet on the bottom rack to collect any oil drippings. Keep it in for an hour, let it cool and you're good to go — even cooking eggs will be a breeze!

Arguably the most versatile pieces of equipment I own, baking sheets are just as handy for roasting meats and vegetables as they are for baking sweet treats. Alex Carballo, chef and partner of Grand Restaurant Group in Southern California, is also a fan: "Sheet pans are thin, lightweight and versatile enough for prepping, holding and baking," he says. And if you prefer hands-off cooking, they're a smart investment. "Sheet trays will bake anything, which will free you up to work on something else or relax and wait for dinner," shares Tondreau.

When it comes to sweet applications, a sheet pan's most obvious use is probably baking cookies, but I've also used mine to make cakes (you can cut out layers or make a large sheet cake), homemade Pop-Tarts and galettes. Pro tip: If I'm baking something runny in a pie or cake pan, I always stick one of these babies underneath to catch any drippings — easier to clean the tray than the bottom of my oven!

Nordic Ware is a trustworthy brand that has never let me down; my pans are old enough to be museum relics at this point, and they still perform just as well as the day I got 'em. (Psst: I tested nine popular brands in search of the best baking sheets , and this one came out on top.)

Before you shell out for larger gear, it's important to consider just how often you'll be using it. Sure, a bulky slushie maker might churn out delicious frozen drinks, but if you only take it out once a year, is it really worth it?

You won't have to wonder about that with an immersion blender — three of the chefs I spoke to sang its praises. "The immersion blender can function as both a standard blender and a hand mixer, all while only requiring one hand, which makes it especially useful," says Carballo. Sramek notes that he uses it for "blending soups and sauces, emulsifying vinaigrettes or aiolis and even aerating eggs for omelettes."

Lota takes things a step further, opting for a handheld blender "with attachments for blending, whipping and chopping." He adds, "With all the attachments, you can use it for almost every meal." That's what I'm talkin' about!

This reasonably priced model made it to our list of the best immersion blenders , and our tester called it "the little engine that could." She adds, "If I told you you could puree soup, make smoothies, dressings and whipped cream, and chop onions and garlic with one appliance for less than 50 bucks, wouldn't you go for it?"

"I had no issue using it on the stove to make soup or in a Pyrex measuring cup to emulsify vinaigrette. I think it's a smart buy for home cooks who want an immersion blender but don't plan to use it daily. It's especially appealing to anyone looking for some of the capabilities of a food processor and stand mixer without the investment." (Yes, it comes with whisk and vegetable chopper attachments, making it an even better value.)

The reviews quoted above reflect the most recent versions at the time of publication.

articles.title: Trump signals possible Pezeshkian meeting at UN as US weighs next move on Iran
articles.summary: Middle East News: US president Donald Trump has signalled he is “probably open” to meeting Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian in New York this week, as the two leaders.
articles.body: US president Donald Trump has signalled he is “probably open” to meeting Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian in New York this week, as the two leaders are set to attend the United Nations General Assembly amid heightened tensions between Washington and Tehran.Asked by Fox News whether he would meet Pezeshkian during the General Assembly, Trump said he would “probably be open” to holding talks with the Iranian president. The remarks come as Trump weighs his next steps on Iran while Tehran has set out conditions for negotiations.Trump is due to address the General Assembly on Tuesday, while Pezeshkian is scheduled to speak on Wednesday, according to Reuters and Iran’s semi-official Mehr news agency. Their simultaneous presence in New York has raised the possibility of direct contact between the two leaders.“The choreography here is going to make for a fairly dramatic moment,” Theo Wold, a former acting assistant attorney general and former White House domestic policy adviser, told Fox News Digital, referring to the planned appearances by Trump and Pezeshkian.Trump’s two-day visit to the UN General Assembly is expected to include a series of bilateral meetings and events with foreign leaders. Reuters reported that his schedule includes meetings with the leaders of Ukraine, the United Kingdom, Japan and Iraq, as well as a meeting with Venezuela’s interim President Delcy Rodriguez. He is also due to meet New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani.The conflict with Iran is expected to feature prominently in Trump’s discussions with leaders of the Gulf Cooperation Council. He is also scheduled to host a reception for the council, where he is expected to meet Rodriguez in person for the first time.The possibility of a Trump-Pezeshkian meeting comes as the wider regional conflict continues to affect energy markets and shipping. Reuters reported that oil prices fell on Sunday amid hopes of US-Iran diplomacy and signs of increased Saudi exports, although tensions remained high following Houthi attacks on Saudi targets.Trump has also said he is in “deciding mode” on Iran and warned that “very big things” could happen, while maintaining that he remains open to diplomacy.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Belarus says no potash left after Trump claims massive deal for fertilizer
articles.summary: Belarus’s authoritarian leader Alexander Lukashenko said Monday that there are no available volumes of fertilizer to send to the U.S. This came after President Trump announced that he was working on a “massive Deal” to buy potash from Minsk at a steep discount amid the trade war with Canada. “Even if we wanted to supply…
articles.body:
Belarus’s authoritarian leader Alexander Lukashenko said Monday that there are no available volumes of fertilizer to send to the U.S. This came after President Trump announced that he was working on a “massive Deal” to buy potash from Minsk at a steep discount amid the trade war with Canada .

“Even if we wanted to supply [potash] to other, Western markets, we simply do not have those volumes — everything is contracted,” Lukashenko said in remarks published by his office on Monday.

At the same time, Trump posted on his social media site Truth Social that the U.S. purchase of potash from Belarus would be “very good news for our Farmers and Ranchers.”

“The United States is working on a massive Deal with respect to the purchase of Potash from Belarus. The pricing would be for substantially less than we are currently paying to Canada,” he posted.

Potash is a key component in fertilizers, and Canada is the world’s largest supplier, with 53 percent of exports going to the U.S. The Canada Press reported that 80 percent of potash used on U.S. farms comes from Canada.

Canadian potash remains exempt from U.S. tariffs on Canada, amid a fraught trade war between the two countries.

But shortages of fertilizer and its rising price are attributed to multiple global conflicts, including Russia’s war against Ukraine, the U.S. war with Iran and the shutdown of the Strait of Hormuz.

The apparent miscommunication between Trump and Lukashenko over potash comes amid a yearlong charm offensive by the Trump administration with Lukashenko, spearheaded by the president’s special envoy for Belarus, John Coale.

Coale is trading U.S. sanctions relief on Belarus for, at least, Lukashenko releasing political prisoners. Coale has secured at least hundreds of people’s freedom, including a Nobel Peace Prize laureate and the husband of the internationally recognized winner of the 2020 presidential election in Belarus.

Lukashenko, nicknamed Europe’s last dictator, is under massive international sanctions for a violent crackdown after rejecting his 2020 presidential election loss, and for supporting Russian President Vladimir Putin’s war against Ukraine and hybrid attacks against Europe.

Coale met with Lukashenko last week and secured the release of 25 prisoners, but that was far below the 200 he had claimed would be released . Human rights monitors, Belarusian dissidents and freed prisoners say Lukashenko is running a carousel, arresting more political opponents to replace the ones he’s released.

Lukashenko denied this in his meeting with Coale and said, “There are no political prisoners in Belarus.”

articles.title: UK prosecutors charge first person for Rwanda genocide
articles.summary: Vincent Brown is ‘alleged to have directed and incited acts of murder and genocide carried out by others’.
articles.body:
Prosecutors have brought the first-ever charges in the United Kingdom against a man for his alleged role in the 1994 Rwanda genocide .

After a seven-year investigation, Vincent Brown, a 65-year-old doctor who was formerly known as Vincent Bajinya, was arrested and charged on Monday with one count of conduct ancillary to genocide and six offences of aiding crimes against humanity in Rwanda, prosecutors and local authorities said.

“The charges relate to allegations that Dr Brown took part in the genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda in 1994,” Frank Ferguson, head of the Crown Prosecution Service’s counterterror division, said in a statement. “He is alleged to have directed and incited acts of murder and genocide carried out by others.”

“This is the first time charges relating to the genocide against the Tutsi in Rwanda have been brought in the United Kingdom,” the statement added.

Brown was first arrested in 2006. His extradition to Rwanda, along with four other men, was refused by a UK court in 2017. Metropolitan police war crimes investigators then began looking into the case in 2019 at the request of the Rwandan government. Several other countries have already prosecuted suspects in the Rwandan genocide .

Originally from Kigali, Brown lives in London, where he once worked for a charity assisting refugee nurses and midwives seeking work in Britain.

He is believed to have entered the UK as an asylum seeker in 1998, former Rwandan Justice Minister Tharcisse Karugarama told the Associated Press news agency in 2006.

The doctor changed his name when granted UK citizenship in 2004, attorney Philip Eldin-Taylor said at the time.

Brown is due to appear at Westminster Magistrates’ Court on Tuesday.

Police said they are continuing to investigate several other Rwandan genocide suspects living in Britain.

“This case demonstrates the UK is not a safe haven for individuals suspected of committing international crimes,” Commander Helen Flanagan, head of counterterror policing, said.

The Rwandan genocide saw an estimated 800,000 people, mostly Tutsis, killed in 100 days of slaughter.

articles.title: Gov Pritzker dodges questions on Hasan Piker, says focus should be on stopping Trump
articles.summary: Gov. JB Pritzker dodged questions about Hasan Piker's controversial stances and influence in the party, insisting Democrats should focus on stopping Trump.
articles.body: Gov. JB Pritzker, D-Ill., avoided multiple questions about far-left streamer Hasan Piker on Sunday as he insisted his focus was on stopping President Donald Trump in his "tracks." "I‘m not focused on the streamers and what they‘re saying. There‘s a whole lot of them and they got a whole lot of views," Pritzker said when asked by ABC's Jonathan Karl if the Democratic Party should outright denounce the streamer, citing Piker's position that Iran having a nuclear weapon would bring more stability to the Middle East. Karl told Pritzker that Piker had a "pretty big following" online. OCASIO-CORTEZ CALLS FOCUS ON HASAN PIKER 'ABSOLUTELY LUDICROUS' AS SOME DEMOCRATS DEMAND DISTANCE "I understand that. I'm just saying that what I think we should be talking about and focused on is how do we stop Donald Trump in his tracks?" Pritzker responded. "How do we make sure that we‘re putting forward an agenda that really fights for the people who need it, which are the most vulnerable, the workers, you know, the middle class who really need someone to stand up for them. That‘s why I‘m a Democrat. That‘s why the Democratic Party exists. That‘s what we should be focused on." Karl asked Pritzker if he would accept an endorsement from Piker, before noting the streamer likely would not endorse the governor. ABDUL EL-SAYED DISMISSES QUESTIONS ABOUT HASAN PIKER TIES ON 'FACE THE NATION,' PIVOTS TO GROCERIES "Again, I‘m not focused. I don‘t even want to talk about it. Hasan Piker doesn‘t mean anything to me or in my election," he said. Piker has done multiple interviews in recent weeks in which he's been asked about some of his controversial political stances. HASAN PIKER SAYS HE’D ‘ABSOLUTELY’ CAMPAIGN FOR AOC IN 2028 AS EL-SAYED DISTANCES HIMSELF "Do you think Iran should be free to build a nuclear weapon?" Axios correspondent Alex Thompson asked in an interview on Thursday. "I think Iran, much like any other sovereign nation, has a right to defend itself, regardless of its domestic policies," Piker responded. The popular Twitch streamer went on to cite political scientist John Mearsheimer in the belief that "mutually assured destruction is the only way for countries to have sovereignty," something he said would bring regional stability. "Now having said that, do I want Iran to have nuclear arms? No. But I also don't want America, or Russia, or China to have nuclear arms either," Piker said. "Do you think the Middle East would be more stable if Iran had a nuclear weapon?" Thompson followed. "I believe yes. I think that the Middle East would be more stable," Piker responded. In the same interview, Piker claimed the U.S. is responsible for more terrorism than al Qaeda "pound for pound." Some Democrats have forcefully rejected Piker, including Rahm Emanuel, who issued a statement on X calling out Piker's positions. "The great thing about America is that everyone is entitled to their opinions and free to express them, however dumb or immoral. That includes ‘Comrade’ Piker. The rest of us are just as free — obligated even — to call out this vile, hateful speech that only divides America," he wrote. CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Political strategist Kaivan Shroff told Fox News Digital in a statement, "Pritzker can say Hasan Piker doesn’t mean anything to him, but that’s increasingly hard to square with reality. Piker is showing up in Senate campaign ads, campaigning with Democratic candidates and publicly talking about his relationship with AOC’s team. At some point ‘he’s just a streamer’ stops being an answer. Streamers are part of the political media ecosystem now." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Democrats have spent years talking about the need to compete with Republicans in the influencer/podcast space. They can’t suddenly pretend influencers are irrelevant when one becomes inconvenient. The question isn’t whether Democrats should spend all day talking about Hasan Piker — of course they shouldn’t — and nor should they let the media’s disproportionate coverage of the issue go unaddressed," Shroff added. "But the real question 2028 candidates will have to answer is … who is in the big tent, and who is out…where is the line? And what angry loud online fanbase are they willing to p--- off in order to stand by their values?"

articles.title: Commanders face critical decision on Jayden Daniels' elbow as specialists review MRI results
articles.summary: Jayden Daniels' MRI results are now being reviewed by specialists who could recommend surgery for his dislocated elbow, potentially ending his season.
articles.body: The results of an MRI done on Jayden Daniels' dislocated left elbow will now go through a rigorous study by specialists to determine exactly what next steps the Washington Commanders should take with their starting quarterback, according to a source. So what does that mean? Daniels will miss Sunday's game against the Seattle Seahawks. Marcus Mariota will start. WASHINGTON COMMANDERS FACE SEASON-DEFINING CRISIS AS JAYDEN DANIELS SUFFERS ANOTHER SERIOUS ELBOW INJURY Interestingly, the Seahawks are optimistic they will get starting quarterback Sam Darnold back for that game, although that is not yet fully certain and will depend on how he looks in practice. Daniels, meanwhile, is getting multiple medical opinions to determine what he should do next. "He had imaging done today," Commanders coach Dan Quinn said. "He'll see specialists early this week, Tuesday and Wednesday, and then we'll go through the process from there. "...Until we go through that process, we just, I'd be guessing to give you any [timeline]." HITS KEEP COMING AS RAMS LOSE MYLES GARRETT FOR AT LEAST FOUR GAMES AFTER LOOMING KNEE SURGERY Quinn is wise not to give a timeline because the specialists might suggest something so drastic as surgery, which would end Daniels' season. Or they could reboot a rehabilitation program similar to the one Daniels underwent last season that avoided surgery altogether. Even a rehab program is probably going to keep Daniels out for weeks. Daniels, who played only seven of 17 games last year, dislocated the same left elbow last season and opted not to have surgery in an effort to try and save the season. CALEB WILLIAMS AVOIDS MAJOR HAMSTRING INJURY AS MRI REVEALS A STRAIN BUT NO TEAR AFTER VIKINGS GAME SCARE He missed three games while he recovered. But he aggravated the injury in Week 14 against and the club basically shut him down the final four games. And here are the lingering questions: Are Daniels and the Commanders going to take the same path, basically doing the same thing, and expecting a different long-term result? Surgery is drastic and rarely needed following an elbow dislocation. But because the details of the Daniels MRI are not known, surgery cannot be ruled out. Surgery is often recommended when the elbow cannot maintain its proper alignment or remains unstable after manually guiding the bones back into place – a non-surgical procedure called a closed reduction. Surgery is also recommended when ligaments, tendons, or joint capsules are severely torn and compromise long-term joint function. But, again, it remains unknown what exactly Daniels is dealing with. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! The Commanders now face the prospect of playing at least one game and probably more with Mariota, and perhaps another quarterback, while Daniels recovers. Losing Daniels is a major blow because Washington’s offense is built around his arm talent, mobility and ability to create opportunities outside the structure of the offense. His absence in the coming weeks (months?) places greater pressure on an already 0–2 team and a coaching staff trying to stabilize a season that has quickly veered off course. articles.title: Putin’s party wins supermajority in Russia’s parliamentary election
articles.summary: Victory of United Russia party strengthens Putin’s hand even as the war with Ukraine grows more unpopular.
articles.body:
President Vladimir Putin’s United Russia party has won a record supermajority in tightly orchestrated parliamentary polls that excluded virtually any genuine opposition, near complete official results show.

With over 58 percent of votes secured, United Russia, which has dominated Russian politics for 25 years, is on track to win more than three quarters of the seats in the lower house, the State Duma, according to the results announced on Monday after three days of voting that ended on Sunday.

The polls were the first parliamentary vote since Russian forces invaded Ukraine in 2022 and the first to include residents of four Ukrainian regions that were seized and illegally annexed by Moscow later that year.

Reporting from Moscow, Al Jazeera’s Dmitry Medvedenko said the results, along with a high voter turnout of almost 60 percent, “is likely to be seen by Moscow as emboldening, as public support for what it is doing, especially for what it’s doing in Ukraine for the continuation of the war”.

Ella Pamfilova, chair of the Central Electoral Commission, said Yabloko, the only registered anti-war party in Russia, did not win any seats at the national level. It had been removed from the ballot last month by Russia’s Supreme Court and only had a few dozen candidates in single-seat races.

Yabloko did enter the regional parliament in western Russia’s Novgorod region. It said on social media that it received about 12,000 votes – just over six percent of votes and enough to enter the regional legislature.

Yabloko and the Communist Party, which has criticised some aspects of government policy but carefully avoided any criticism of Putin, said many of their observers were turned away from polling stations.

The Communists made it into parliament with 13.8 percent of the vote, securing 40 Duma seats. The nationalist LDPR party won 25 seats and the New People party 20.

Russia did not invite observers from the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE), which the Foreign Ministry has accused of “double standards” for its criticism of the country. OSCE Parliamentary Assembly President Pere Joan Pons said the decision to exclude observers violated Russia’s commitments as a member.

Many Russians appeared unsurprised by the poll results.

“In the morning, I saw that ⁠⁠United Russia was winning. It probably comes as a surprise to nobody,” said Moscow resident Tatyana.

Asked what she would like to change, she said: “Well, I guess everyone knows the most acute thing – the conflict in Ukraine. I’d like to see it end sooner, with peaceful methods if possible”.

The continuation of the war risks entrenching policies, which are increasingly affecting average Russians and the parliamentary supermajority may struggle to change the dynamic.

“Putin, of course, will interpret United Russia’s results as confirmation of the (public) support of the war, even though it is not the case: The overall demand for ending the war is growing,” said Tatyana Stanovaya of the Carnegie Russia Eurasia Center in an online commentary.

“The main question is: What now? There are great concerns about mobilisation, new repressions, harsher measures and escalation,” she wrote.

The EU’s top diplomat Kaja Kallas dismissed Russia’s “so-called” election.

“The Kremlin silenced dissent, barred the only registered party that opposed its war in Ukraine and shut out international election monitors. The veneer of democracy is all that remains in Russia,” Kallas said.

In a joint statement, five countries, including Australia, Britain and Canada, condemned Russia’s “sham” parliamentary elections in areas of occupied Ukraine, branding them “part of a wider system of occupation”.

articles.title: A Washington family has farmed the same land for more than 70 years as a dairy, hay farm and agritourism business; nearly 40 acres can now never be developed even though the family keeps ownership
articles.summary: US News: For more than seven decades, the Foster family has worked the same stretch of Washington farmland, raising dairy cattle, producing hay and opening its.
articles.body: For more than seven decades, the Foster family has worked the same stretch of Washington farmland, raising dairy cattle, producing hay and opening its operation to visitors through agritourism. Now, nearly 40 acres of that family-owned property will remain farmland permanently, giving the land a future that extends well beyond the current generation, states an online press release by Forterra Org. Scroll down to read the details of the farm owned by Brian and Connie Foster.Nearly 40 acres protected foreverThe farmland along State Route 530 NE in the Stillaguamish Valley has been placed under permanent conservation through a partnership involving Forterra and Snohomish County, with support from the Stillaguamish Tribe of Indians, states the press release. As per the release, the agreement prevents future development on the protected acreage while allowing the Foster family to retain ownership. The land can continue to be farmed, but its conservation status means it cannot be converted to residential or other development in the future.For a family that has worked the property for more than 70 years, the arrangement preserves both the land and its role in the valley's agricultural landscape. The protected parcels sit next to the Portage Creek Wildlife Area and within a designated Flood Hazard Zone critical area, making their undeveloped status significant beyond agriculture alone.A working farm with environmental benefitsAs per the release, conserving the property also helps maintain an important piece of the Stillaguamish Valley's floodplain. Keeping the acreage open can contribute to flood management by preserving land that can absorb and slow floodwaters, states the release. The undeveloped farmland can also help reduce pollution and agricultural runoff reaching downstream waterways.Rather than removing the property from private use, the conservation easement creates a middle ground: the Fosters retain ownership and can continue farming while agreeing to permanent restrictions on development. That approach has become an important tool for protecting working farms in areas where agricultural land faces increasing development pressure, explains the online press release.A broader effort in the Stillaguamish ValleyThe Foster property is part of a larger conservation effort involving Forterra, Snohomish County, the Stillaguamish Tribe and local landowners. Funding for the easements came through Snohomish County's Conservation Futures program, along with support from the Stillaguamish Tribe through the Washington Department of Ecology's Floodplains by Design grant program, informs the release. The funding supports projects designed to improve floodplain restoration and resilience.The Foster family now joins other landowners in the valley who have used conservation easements to keep farmland and habitat protected while allowing properties to remain privately owned. For the Stillaguamish Valley, those individual agreements add up to a larger effort to maintain agricultural land, preserve habitat and protect the natural functions of the floodplain.Part of a statewide conservation recordThe latest agreement is also one piece of Forterra's broader conservation work. The organization has completed nearly 500 conservation transactions across Washington, protecting more than 275,000 acres, informs the release. In Snohomish County alone, Forterra holds or has helped facilitate more than a dozen conservation easements. The organization also monitors more than 100 easement properties each year to make sure the agreed-upon conservation protections remain intact.For the Foster family, the nearly 40 acres represent something more tangible, a farmland that can stay in the family while remaining farmland for generations to come.Image Courtesy: istockCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: I didn't go to war so...: Hindu American Army veteran Ruchir Bakshi pushes back hatred, slams call to 'tear down' Texas Hanuman statue
articles.summary: US News: US Army veteran Ruchir Bakshi strongly reacted to the nonstop hate mongering on social media targeting Hindus and Hindu religious figures and said he .
articles.body: US Army veteran Ruchir Bakshi strongly reacted to the nonstop hate mongering on social media targeting Hindus and Hindu religious figures and said he did not go to war for a country that comes after his religion. Bakshi was deployed to Afghanistan and Iraq and his service included combat-zone assignments in southern Afghanistan and around Baghdad. Bakshi reacted to a YouTuber's now-viral post of the 'Statue of Union', the 90-foot-tall statue of Lord Hanuman at the Sri Ashtalakshmi Temple in Sugar Land, Texas. "Btw, when we win, we are tearing this down," Jesse Hughes, the YouTuber, wrote without specifying what win he meant, as Texas is a red state."I’m a US Army combat veteran and a Hindu American. I didn’t put on that uniform, leave my family, and go to war so some third-rate talk show guy could announce that when his side “wins,” they’re coming for my religion," Bakshi wrote.Calling this a threat to Hinduism, Bakshi said those who worship in these temples pay taxes, run businesses, and send their sons and daughters to the same Army where he served. A call for vandalism is not patriotism, he said."I served with Christians, Jews, Muslims, atheists, and other Hindus. Nobody pulled rank on God before we went outside the wire. Some of those men never came home. None of them died so you could fantasize about ravaging someone else’s faith. The people who worship in those temples pay taxes, run businesses, and send their sons and daughters into the same Army I served in. “When we win, we are tearing this down” is not patriotism. It is a threat against Hinduism itself to vandalize another American community’s house of worship because you hate the faith inside it," Bakshi said."If winning in America means demolishing Hindu temples, you don’t want the country I fought for. You just want a license to go after people who aren’t you. America is not your theocracy. Religious liberty does not expire for Hindus when you decide you’ve won. You don’t get to tear anything down. Not legally. Not morally. Not in the country for which I actually sacrificed," Bakshi wrote.But Bakshi was also not spared from trolling. "Your service in the military does not grant you a mandate to redefine the foundational nature of this nation, nor does it make the demographic and spiritual displacement of my people a matter of settled law," one wrote."Hiding behind service is low. Rome let barbarians serve in their military and those barbarians still turned on Rome. Your service doesnt prove loyalty. Your idea of America is a false one. It's a contemporary fabrication based on a 1908 play," another wrote.Social media users told him that Americans don't consider him tobe American as he served is the US Army only to become a citizen.Coalition of Hindus of North America (CoHNA) responded to Bakshi's social media post and condemned the open religious bigotry on X. "So grateful for your service Ruchir ji. You inspire our entire team. We share your horror at the open religious bigotry being mainstreamed on this platform and are proud to fight it alongside you," CoHNA wrote.Who is Jesse Hughes?Jesse Hughes is a YouTuber, not widely known before his incendiary comment on Hindu idols. He is a Conservative commentator, and after gaining virality, he doubled down on what he meant. He said Christianity is a religion of smashing false idols and added that when Christ returns, all the statues will come down.Who is Rucir Bakshi?Ruchir Bakshi came to the US in 1992 when he was not even 21 years old. After working at a gas station, he joined the US Army Reserves after his family also settled in the US. After September 11, 2001, he was sent to Afghanistan. He called himself a Republican initially but then became a Democrat. Bakshi is an instructional designer and AI evangelist who builds practical, measurable learning for higher education and Department of War programs.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Karl Bushby left Chile in 1998 to walk home to Hull; 28 years later, he will swim the English Channel to finish
articles.summary: UK News: Karl Bushby left Chile in 1998 with a simple rule: walk home to Hull, and never use transport. Twenty-eight years and 30,516 miles later, he is now in.
articles.body: Karl Bushby left Chile in 1998 with a simple rule: walk home to Hull, and never use transport. Twenty-eight years and 30,516 miles later, he is now in Belgium with one stretch of water left. According to the BBC, Eurotunnel refused him use of its service tunnel this summer on safety grounds, but French authorities have now permitted him to swim the 21-mile-wide English Channel. The 57-year-old former paratrooper plans to enter the water on 1 October, weather and tides permitting, and expects the crossing to take three or four days. He aims to be back home in Hull by 1 November.Why did Karl Bushby leave Chile in 1998 to walk home to HullBushby began the expedition in 1998, setting out from Chile and travelling towards Hull under a self-imposed rule that prevents him from using transport. He had covered 30,516 miles (49,110km) by September 2026, with his route including the Bering Strait between Alaska and Russia and the Darién Gap between Colombia and Panama.Bushby is a former paratrooper, and his journey has included crossing the frozen Bering Strait. He spent months waiting for suitable weather conditions while navigating shifting ice and avoiding polar bears. His route was subsequently affected by Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, leaving him unable to enter Russia or Iran and forcing him to find another way forward.Why was Karl Bushby refused permission to use the Channel TunnelBushby had hoped to use the Channel Tunnel to avoid crossing the English Channel by water. Eurotunnel said in June that closing its service tunnel, which runs alongside the main tunnel, would create a safety risk for passengers and interfere with essential maintenance work. Bushby described the arrangements needed to return to the UK as difficult, saying: “Organising how I'm going to get back into the UK has been a nightmare.”Bushby had asked Eurotunnel for permission to use a service tunnel but was refused on safety and operational grounds. He then said his team had obtained support from within the French government for an alternative crossing. “It looks like we’ve managed to figure that out,” Bushby said, referring to the permission to swim from France.How did Karl Bushby get French permission to swimThe BBC reported on 5 September 2026 that Bushby says he has permission from French authorities to swim the English Channel. He said he expected to enter the water on 1 October, provided tides and weather conditions allowed it. His Los Angeles-based team had been in discussions with French authorities over the crossing.According to The Yorkshire Post, Bushby said a French law dating from 1993 had presented an obstacle because it prohibited swimming from the French coast. He said his team had eventually found support within the French government. The BBC reported that Bushby expected the Channel swim to take “three or four days”, with rest periods between swimming sessions on a support boat.How did Karl Bushby cross the Caspian Sea in 2024Bushby has previous experience of long-distance swimming. In 2024 he swam about 186 miles (300km) across the Caspian Sea, according to the BBC. The Yorkshire Post reports the swim lasted 31 days and involved members of the Azerbaijani coastguard and two swimmers from the national team.The English Channel crossing will present a different set of conditions. The Yorkshire Post notes the Channel is 21 miles wide and that strong tides and September water temperatures of 17–19C make the crossing demanding. Bushby told the BBC that he had not had time to train specifically for the latest challenge because he had been concentrating on planning the route.With the French permission secured, Bushby said he was returning to Europe to continue from where he had stopped in Belgium. Reportedly, he was aiming to reach Hull by 1 November, while the Yorkshire Post said he expected to arrive at his mother’s home in about two months. “It’s all about getting the job done and getting home alive,” Bushby told the BBC.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Will Earl Spencer's Diana book damage the monarchy?
articles.summary: What more revelations are going to appear now the full details of his Diana book are published?
articles.body:
A slanging match doesn't usually do either side much good. Unless you're selling books, when a controversy can be extremely helpful.

Earl Spencer's book about his sister, Diana, has had six days of public accusations and counter-claims, with extensive news coverage.

So perhaps it's not surprising that even before it's officially published, Swan Song: Diana, My Sister is racing up the Amazon best-seller chart.

It's likely to be the most significant royal book since Prince Harry's startling 2023 memoir, Spare, and Andrew Lownie's 2025 book Entitled, which doomed Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor's reputation.

Key takeaways from BBC interview as Earl Spencer defends claims about King

'I'm telling the truth': Earl Spencer defends Diana book claims about Charles in BBC interview

Bitter row over Diana book brings back unhappy times for royals

The coverage has been driven by a simple question: should we believe Earl Spencer's claims about the King's callousness after Diana's death ? Or should we believe the unusually robust denial from Buckingham Palace?

But when you read further through the book, there's a more complicated story being told.

Earl Spencer is the brother watching events unfolding in the strange and ultimately doomed life of his sister, who has stepped from being his childhood companion to become one of the most famous women in the world.

He describes a kind of grief and irritation as Diana becomes public property and then royal property, which irks him even more, disliking the "nonsense of fawning" around the monarchy.

It's a stark reminder that Diana was only just 20 years old when she married - becoming a global superstar - and was dead 16 years later.

Earl Spencer depicts her as a caring, generous character who was haunted by self-doubt, dogged by eating disorders, lacking in warmth from her new royal family and then ultimately dragged down by the tabloid media.

"She craved acceptance, admiration, kindness, and - perhaps above all - love," writes Charles Spencer about Diana.

"She got stuck into gritty, controversial, but crucial causes partly because she had a fine, natural social conscience, but also to assuage nagging feelings of worthlessness."

And with a memoir like this it will be the extra details that will fascinate people.

The stepmother to Diana and Charles, Raine Spencer, is painted in an unflattering light, and Diana is described as getting so angry once that she pushed Raine down the staircase at their home in Althorp. "Raine fortunately landed flush on her buttocks, rather than on bone, and got up, leaving the saloon without a backwards glance," he writes. It was in response, says the book, to Raine telling Diana: "I have always felt so very sorry for the Prince of Wales, marrying someone quite as stupid as you."

There's not a single mention of Meghan, the Duchess of Sussex, even though she was talked about in the TV interviews

We're told that a "nephew" wanted Earl Spencer to be in a documentary about Diana, which will raise speculation about Prince Harry's plans for his mother's 30th anniversary next year

The book recounts that she disliked Dodi Fayed's father, Mohammed Fayed, accusing him of crudely groping her

Diana's preferences included the soap opera Crossroads and the music of David Bowie. She'd watched The Sound of Music 16 times and the paper she read was the Daily Mail

Earl Spencer will ultimately be remembered by the passionate eulogy he delivered at Diana's funeral in Westminster Abbey.

He reveals how he had pretended to have lost his copy of his speech at the rehearsal, so no one could hear it in advance and try to tone down his stinging criticism of the press and the royals.

After the hounding of Diana by the paparazzi, he says he personally rang tabloid newspaper editors to disinvite them from the Abbey funeral, after their invitations had already been sent out.

She was buried on an island in the Spencers' Althorp estate, rather than a graveyard - and the book describes how a bishop was brought to consecrate the ground to make it possible.

Much of the interest in this book has been driven by its settling of old scores with the Royal Family. It can feel like medieval barons jousting.

References to King Charles are almost all negative, including the suggestion that he was jealous of his wife's public popularity.

The book reports a conversation in which it's claimed the then-Prince Charles complained: "I mean, I'm 43,' he said, 'and I employ fifty people' – he was flushed in the face now – 'but my parents insist on treating me like – like a child!'"

The King is portrayed as resentful, with a "senior courtier" reporting an alleged comment by the late Queen: "He even resented it when I taught him the alphabet."

There's a bizarre account of discussions in the Royal Family about whether the then-Prince Charles's ears should have been pinned back.

And there's the allegation that Diana had said the King was in love with his valet, which the author himself says seemed improbable.

What comes across is how close the Spencers were to the royals - but without being friends.

Charles and Diana Spencer went to the same children's parties as the young royals.

The royals are depicted as the type of children who come round, break your toys and then disappear, in what might be an extended metaphor for how he saw Diana's story.

There's also a story about a teenage Prince Andrew smirking in a church service because the priest used the word "womb".

While the TV interviews have sought Spencer's views on Prince Harry and Prince William, the book doesn't go there.

Earl Spencer describes his opposition to the boys having to walk behind the coffin at their mother's funeral - and he talks of "how tiny, and slight, and bereft, Harry looked".

But the focus of this book is much more about the Diana era - and an elegy to the lost world of their childhood.

Earl Spencer emphasises its country house happiness, with dens, dogs and horses, but it's also dotted with cruelty, with violent nannies and the "mindless and often destructive" tradition of boarding schools.

A boy who accidentally shot and killed his father gets the mawkish nickname "Baghdad".

Although the book is about Diana, it's also about its author, the younger brother trying to make sense of what's happened - and also, like many younger brothers, being able to criticise without being able to take responsibility.

Earl Spencer talks about how little he cares for "archaic" titles for the aristocracy or royals.

And in this book, the title that seems really to have shaped his life most is "Diana's brother".

Swan Song: Diana, My Sister, by Charles Spencer. Published by Penguin.

articles.title: 2 battling fire at Yosemite killed in helicopter crash
articles.summary: Two members of a helicopter crew battling the Dome Fire in Yosemite National Park were killed in a crash on Sunday, the U.S Forest Service said.
articles.body: Two members of a helicopter crew battling the Dome Fire in Yosemite National Park were killed in a crash on Sunday, the U.S Forest Service said. The two pilots, who have not been publicly identified, were the only people on board and were conducting fire suppression operations in the national park, said Adrienne Freeman, a U.S. Forest Service spokesperson. Both the NTSB and FAA said they are investigating. The FAA confirmed the crash occurred around 3 p.m. Sunday and involved a Eurocopter AS32 helicopter. A spokesperson for the NTSB said its personnel will be on scene “when fire conditions allow.” The aviation company Fly Precision said the pilots were part of its team. “It is with unimaginable sadness and broken hearts that we share the loss of two beloved members of our team,” the company said in a statement Sunday. “We ask for privacy and compassion for their families and our team as we grieve this tremendous loss.” On Monday, the Dome Fire, which started in Mariposa, California, on September 15, was larger than 3,000 acres and only 15% contained, according to wildfire authorities. The fire “continued to spread at a moderate rate of growth” and has swept further into the 2017 Empire Fire footprint, officials said. The cause of the fire is under investigation, authorities said. The NTSB spokesperson said a preliminary report on the helicopter crash will be released within the next 30 days.

articles.title: Arrests as migrant boat reaches Folkestone without being intercepted
articles.summary: Five people have been detained and an investigation launched, the Home Office says.
articles.body:
Five people have been detained and sent to border security command after a migrant boat reached Kent without being intercepted.

The dinghy made it to shore at Folkestone on Monday morning. The Home Office says an investigation has begun.

All on the boat are believed to have been accounted for.

The thousands of migrants who cross the Channel are usually brought to shore by border security command or RNLI boats but this one is thought to have slipped through undetected.

No small boat arrivals to the UK coast without an escort have been officially recorded since 6 September, 2025.

Kent Police said it became aware of the incident at about 09:25 BST on Monday.

"Patrols attended and five people were detained and passed to border security command officers," the force said.

The Home Office called the incident "isolated and rare".

It said: "Officers responded quickly, detaining five individuals. There is an ongoing investigation and it would be inappropriate to comment further."

Also on Monday, people in life jackets were pictured being taken into the border security command compound in Dover.

Other migrant dinghies were also believed to be in the Channel, with French lifeboat and navy vessels tracking one as far west as Normandy.

Some 17,480 migrants have arrived after crossing the Channel by boat so far this year, including 5,011 since Andy Burnham became Prime Minister.

The 2026 total is down 46% on this time last year.

articles.title: Former ‘death squad’ leader appears in military trial in The Gambia
articles.summary: Sanna Manjang faces court for deserting army in 2017 after end of Jammeh’s 20-year rule.
articles.body:
The former head of the Gambian paramilitary unit known as the “Junglers” has appeared in a military court to face charges of desertion.

Sanna Manjang is accused of deserting the armed forces when the lieutenant colonel fled the country in 2017 after the end of the 20-year rule of President Yahya Jammeh.

The case in the capital, Banjul, marks another official bid at accountability for killings which happened when Jammeh was in power, after a murder case against Manjang was dropped in July.

He is facing trial for an absence of “a continuous period of nine years with the intention of deserting”. Manjang was arrested in Senegal last November and was repatriated to The Gambia a month later.

The Junglers armed group, which operated independently from the Gambian army, has long been accused by the United Nations of extrajudicial killings and torture.

Longtime leader Jammeh was forced into exile after losing power in 2016 to Adama Barrow, then opposition leader and now president.

Following Jammeh’s departure, the country established the Truth, Reconciliation and Reparations Commission (TRRC). It investigated alleged crimes under his rule and found that between 240 and 250 people were killed by the state. It also found evidence of widespread extrajudicial killings, torture, kidnappings, witch hunts and other abuses.

Several of Jammeh’s accomplices, including Junglers, have been detained and sentenced abroad in Germany, Switzerland and the United States.

Manjang was previously charged with four counts of murder, including that of AFP journalist Deyda Hydara in 2004, but the charges were dropped in July as The Gambia struggled to summon witnesses, some allegedly members of the death squad.

In addition to Hydara’s shooting, Manjang was accused of killing three other men, including one he personally decapitated.

After the charges were dropped, Manjang was charged separately for the assault of two other men in an ongoing trial.

articles.title: Venezuelan man shot by ICE in Texas says he’s in pain and still has bullet in his back
articles.summary: Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez spoke from detention as lawmakers and advocates said he’s the victim of an ICE shooting and its “key witness” and shouldn’t be deported.
articles.body: AUSTIN, Texas — The Venezuelan man shot by ICE in Austin during a traffic stop spoke from immigration detention Monday and said he was in a lot of pain and still had a bullet lodged in his back. Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez, 28, was shot early Sunday afternoon by an ICE officer while making deliveries as a DoorDash driver. He is being held in immigration custody at the South Texas ICE Processing Center in Pearsall, Texas. Garcés Pérez said by phone during a news conference Monday that he was shot near the clavicle and that he has not received the medical attention he needs. He said doctors did not remove the bullet because it was close to his spine and ICE was pushing the hospital to release him into the agency’s custody in a hurry. Garcés Pérez said he arrived at the detention center around 4 a.m., where he complained about his ongoing pain. He said he did not receive medical treatment at the detention center or pain relief when he arrived until he was given an unknown pill Monday morning. He added that he had to sleep on the floor in a cold room. Lawmakers, advocates and Garcés Pérez’s attorney demanded his release, alleging he was taken from a hospital into custody within four hours with a bullet still lodged in his back. “Wilber is a victim of the shooting and the most important witness to it. You do not deport the key witness to your own officer’s use of force,” Juan Proaño, the CEO of the League of United Latin American Citizens, said during a news conference Monday afternoon that was also attended by Garcés Pérez’s wife. A spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, the federal agency to which ICE belongs, said in a statement late Sunday that Garcés Pérez was in stable condition and was in federal custody pending removal from the U.S. A senior administration official told NBC News on Monday that Garcés Pérez did not have a criminal history beyond being in the country illegally. According to Garcés Pérez’s attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, he entered the country legally and was seeking asylum. She said Garcés Pérez told her he had let the immigration court know when he had a change of address, but a notice to appear in court was sent to an old address. Because of this mistake, Garcés Pérez missed his court hearing and was ordered deported in absentia, according to his attorney. Lincoln-Goldfinch shared Garcés Pérez’s account of the shooting, saying he was making a delivery when “an unmarked black truck sideswiped him.” “He didn’t know it was ICE, and he did a U-turn under the highway. The truck chased him and sideswiped him again, and the agents came out and shot him in the back of the neck and pulled him out of the car,” she said. DHS did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the statements made during the news conference or for comment on earlier statements made by Lincoln-Goldfinch. Rep. Greg Casar, D-Texas, said Monday that “the federal government should not be allowed to shoot you and then disappear you from the country so that no one can be held responsible.” “I am demanding, and Congress is making very clear to the head of ICE and to Secretary Mullin, that Wilber Garcés needs to be released to medical care and should not be in Pearsall,” he said, referring to Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin. “He needs to be released right now.” A social media video verified by NBC News captures the sound of tires screeching followed by a person exiting a dark-colored SUV as a blue sedan is stopped next to it, both vehicles facing each other. The sedan also appears to be damaged on the passenger side. At least three gunshots are heard as the person approaches the sedan and runs up to it as it slowly lurches forward. The video shows the person standing next to the sedan’s driver’s side as it stops in front of an intersection. Another video shows the blue sedan with its driver’s side door open and Garcés Pérez hunched over in the driver’s seat, holding his left upper chest, near his shoulder, as multiple law enforcement officers gather around. The woman taking the video says, “Why did he do that to him?” The officers tell her that an ambulance is coming. The video shows Garcés Pérez being taken out of the car and handcuffed behind his back. The agents make him sit on the ground. There appears to be a large bloodstain down his back. The officers cut open the back of his shirt, revealing a bullet hole. An officer asks the woman taking the video if she saw what happened. In Spanish, she replies that “they just shot him because he didn’t want to stop” his vehicle. “This is unjust,” she says as she’s recording the video. A Texas Department of Public Safety spokesperson said the agency had received a request for assistance from ICE for a vehicle pursuit involving a blue Toyota Corolla. Lincoln-Goldfinch said earlier she was with Garcés Pérez’s wife at the hospital where he was taken, hoping to get information on his condition, but they were escorted from the premises. “We not only were lied to and told that he wasn’t there, but we were thrown off the hospital grounds by several officers who treated us as trespassers,” she said. DHS has not provided any information about whether the ICE officer involved was wearing a body camera or if Garcés Pérez was the target of an operation. Local officials at the news conference decried the increase in arrests in their state and called for an independent investigation into the shooting. Austin police are investigating. Police Chief Lisa Davis said Monday that the investigation will be impartial and based on the facts. She did not have additional information to share about the shooting. “I understand that that is frustrating. I also recognize the concern and uncertainty this incident has created in our community,” she said in a video statement. “But it is important that we distinguish between what we know, what we have heard and what the evidence ultimately establishes.” The shooting comes as ICE has greatly increased enforcement across the country this summer, making more than 50,000 arrests a month for the first time in its history in July and August. It also comes two months after an ICE officer fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a Mexican national, in Houston during an attempted traffic stop to conduct an immigration arrest. DHS has said Salgado Araujo was in the country illegally and attempted to run over agents, but it has not provided evidence of its claims. About a week after the fatal shooting in Houston, another ICE officer shot and killed Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine, after a traffic stop. Neither man was ICE’s intended target during the immigration operations.

articles.title: Bishop of Lincoln resigns amid sexual assault inquiry
articles.summary: The Right Reverend Stephen Conway remains under investigation following a "safeguarding complaint".
articles.body:
The Bishop of Lincoln, the Right Reverend Stephen Conway, has resigned amid an ongoing investigation into an allegation of sexual assault.

Conway's resignation, which will formally come into effect on 1 October, was confirmed in a statement from the Church of England.

"The complaint process is ongoing. Clergy remain subject to church disciplinary procedures following resignation or retirement," it said.

Conway had been suspended from ministry in February when a "safeguarding complaint" was made.

At the time, Lincolnshire Police said the arrest was part of an "ongoing investigation following an allegation that a man was sexually assaulted between 2018 and 2025".

Following Conway's resignation, the Church said Dr Nicholas Chamberlain, the Bishop of Grantham, would continue as Acting Bishop of Lincoln until a permanent replacement is chosen.

articles.title: Italian PM pushes foreign student cap in classrooms, burqa, niqab ban in schools
articles.summary: Giorgia Meloni's proposed legislation would cap foreign students per classroom and ban burqas and niqabs in Italian schools to foster integration.
articles.body: Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced plans Sept. 20 to introduce legislation capping the number of foreign students in Italian classrooms and banning face-covering garments, including burqas and niqabs, in schools. The conservative leader said her proposed measures aim to foster integration, preserve Italian cultural identity and ensure that native children do not feel sidelined in the classroom. "There’s no way that in an Italian classroom, the ones who feel marginalized are Italian children because they have become a minority," Meloni said during a speech to Gioventù Nazionale, the youth wing of her conservative Brothers of Italy party, in Rome, according to reports. SWEDEN VOTES AS MIGRATION, CRIME AND ECONOMY DOMINATE HIGH-STAKES ELECTION Under the proposal, individual classrooms would have limits on non-Italian students to prevent heavy concentrations in specific districts. Meloni did not specify the exact cap but said the government would also require mandatory Italian-language lessons for parents of foreign pupils who struggle to integrate. "For us, anyone who comes to Italy and wants to build their future here must learn our language, understand our culture, and respect our rules," Meloni said, The Associated Press reported. "It is the only serious way to welcome them." Students who don't hold Italian citizenship account for around 11.6% of school enrollment nationwide, according to Italy’s Education Ministry cited by the ISMU ETS Foundation. Under Italian law, children born to foreign parents also do not automatically gain citizenship at birth and must wait until age 18 before they can apply. RUBIO MEETS MELONI AS TRUMP–POPE CLASH CLASH ESCALATES US STRAINS WITH KEY EUROPEAN ALLY Meloni argued that high concentrations of non-native speakers impact the learning process for everyone involved. "If in a classroom there is only one child who doesn’t understand Italian, it is possible that that child will manage, with the help of his peers and teachers, to learn the language and integrate fast," she said. "But if these children are many, or even the majority, that’s not integration anymore, that’s abandonment." The proposed package also targets religious face coverings, explicitly prohibiting burqas and niqabs in educational institutions while permitting other forms of Islamic dress, such as the hijab. In a series of posts on X on Monday, the Brothers of Italy party reinforced the prime minister’s message: "Those who choose to build their future in Italy must learn our language, know our culture, and respect our rules. "School is attended with one's face uncovered. No tradition can impose on a young woman the obligation to hide herself." TRUMP SAYS MELONI 'WANTS TO BE FRIENDS AGAIN' AFTER ITALY REFUSED TO HELP US AMID IRAN WAR A subsequent post added: "Limit on the number of foreign students in classrooms, obligation for parents of pupils with serious integration difficulties to learn Italian, and ban on burqas and niqabs in educational institutions. "Integration comes through knowledge of our language, respect for our rules, and protection of our cultural identity." Several European neighbors, including France and Belgium, have previously imposed bans on face-coverings in public places, though enforcement and legal frameworks differ. The proposed Italian legislation is expected to be considered by Italy’s Council of Ministers before being sent to Parliament for consideration. Meloni, who has led Brothers of Italy since 2014 and served as president of the European Conservatives and Reformists Party from 2020 to 2025, has governed Italy since 2022. articles.title: NFL star Charles Leno Jr. gave $450,000 to his California high school; his donation helped fund a nearly $1 million athletic renovation
articles.summary: US News: Former NFL offensive tackle Charles Leno Jr. has returned to the California high school that helped launch his football career, donating $450,000 towa.
articles.body: Former NFL offensive tackle Charles Leno Jr. has returned to the California high school that helped launch his football career, donating $450,000 toward a new professional-grade turf field at San Leandro High School. The donation formed part of a nearly $1 million renovation of the school's athletic facility at Burrell Field. Leno, who grew up in Oakland and graduated from San Leandro High in 2009, was honoured at the school's homecoming game in October 2025, when he saw the completed field in person for the first time. The new turf is bright blue, a deliberate reference to both of Leno's alma maters, San Leandro High and Boise State University, whose football stadium is known for its blue playing surface. Leno spent a decade in the NFL with the Chicago Bears and Washington Commanders before his playing career ended in 2023.The blue turf connects San Leandro to Boise StateThe colour of the new field was not chosen at random. Leno played college football at Boise State after graduating from San Leandro High, and the school is famous for its blue turf at Albertsons Stadium. Leno said he wanted his contribution to leave something lasting at his former high school and saw the field as a way to connect the 2 stages of his football career. When KTVU asked whether blue was simply his favourite colour, Leno joked that it should be, saying he was fully committed to the idea.The connection was also part of the field's design. Contemporary reporting by the San Leandro Times noted that the new surface was intended to match the San Leandro Pirates' colours while drawing inspiration from Leno's time at Boise State. Leno's college career lasted from 2009 to 2013. He started 39 consecutive games at Boise State and was selected in the seventh round of the 2014 NFL Draft by the Chicago Bears. He later received a Pro Bowl selection in 2018 before joining Washington in 2021.His former coach helped put him on the football pathSan Leandro High football coach Brad Bowers, known as Coach Boom, remains involved with the school's athletes. Bowers told KTVU that Leno had been a basketball player before he recruited him to football. That decision became an important turning point in Leno's career. After playing at San Leandro High, he moved on to Boise State and eventually spent 10 seasons in the NFL.Bowers has remained in contact with Leno, who has returned to the school to speak with current players and has participated in a youth football camp. He told KTVU that Leno's continued involvement has given current students an opportunity to hear directly from someone who came through the same programme. Leno has also described his connection to the school in personal terms. He recalled watching former San Leandro High player Jarrad Page speak to students when Leno was beginning to play football, saying the experience inspired him even though Page did not know it at the time. Leno said he now wants to provide a similar source of inspiration for younger players.The renovation is meant for more than footballThe new surface is not limited to the school's football programme. KTVU reported that the upgraded facility will also serve sports including soccer and track and field. Students and coaches have also pointed to differences between the new surface and the previous field. Senior Nathaniel Brunson told KTVU that turf burns had been a problem on the old field, while Leno said the new surface felt more forgiving when making cuts and other movements.The project was completed over the summer before Leno returned for the school's homecoming game. San Leandro High's school district said the donation helped bring new life to Burrell Field, while local reporting described the project as a major upgrade after more than a decade with the previous artificial turf. The renovation also gave the school an opportunity to honour one of its most prominent former athletes. During the homecoming ceremony, San Leandro High announced that Leno's No. 77 jersey would be retired.Leno has built a record of community givingThe Burrell Field donation is part of a broader record of charitable work by Leno and his wife through their organisation, Beyond the Entertainer. The NFL Players Association named Leno its Week 17 Community MVP in 2022 after his annual Leno Claus initiative. During 25 consecutive days of giving that December, Leno and his organisation supported families, schools, patients and charities, with the NFLPA reporting more than $95,000 in donations.It was not his first Community MVP recognition. The NFLPA said Leno had also received the award in 2020 and 2021. He received it again in 2023 after another 25-day Leno Claus campaign, making him a 4-time NFLPA Community MVP. His return to San Leandro High extends that work to the community where his football career began. For the school, the result is a new blue playing surface that connects Leno's high school and college careers while giving current students a renovated athletic facility.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: U.K. to offer Saudi Arabia aerial refueling to counter Houthi attacks
articles.summary: ABOARD THE BRITISH PRIME MINISTER’S PLANE — Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that Britain has agreed to provide limited military support to Saudi Arabia to repeal attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen.
articles.body: ABOARD THE BRITISH PRIME MINISTER’S PLANE — Prime Minister Andy Burnham said Monday that Britain has agreed to provide limited military support to Saudi Arabia to repeal attacks by Iran-backed Houthi rebels in Yemen. Burnham told reporters as he flew to the United Nations General Assembly in New York that he had agreed the Royal Air Force will provide air-to-air refueling of Saudi planes. The agreement is for a matter of weeks, but Burnham said it will be kept under review. The conflict between the Houthis and Yemen’s Saudi-backed government has reignited, with Houthis aiming missile and drone strikes on Saudi Arabia, including one that targeted Riyadh on Saturday before being intercepted. The Houthis also declared a blockade on Saudi shipping in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait and the Red Sea, attacking Saudi-linked vessels and oil facilities inside the kingdom, the world’s top oil exporter. The Houthis advanced inside Yemen earlier this month, seizing the crucial port city of Mokha and key Red Sea islands allowing them to better monitor shipping traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb, through which some 12% of world trade normally passes. Burnham said he was “acting to secure the interests of Britain and the wider region, because of course Saudi Arabia has been experiencing attack, is looking at potential further disruption, and we need to keep those pathways (for oil) open.” Britain has condemned the Houthi attacks and said the U.K. will “work with partners to support regional stability, protect civilians and support humanitarian access.” U.K. officials had previously declined to comment on “operational matters” but noted that Britain and Saudi Arabia have a close defense partnership. The U.S., which bombed the Houthis under the Biden and Trump administrations, has shown no interest in getting involved military this time around. one more sentence: U.K. officials say the agreement will start in the coming days, and involve one RAF Voyager refueling Saudi planes on “defensive” missions. The Associated Press reported last week that Saudi Arabia has asked its allies, including France, Britain, Pakistan and Egypt to deploy air-defense support to the region to help defend against missiles and drones fired by Houthis and other Iran-backed groups on the kingdom.
